titre_page: How to add lights, shadows and a day and night cycle in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Make your game come alive in Yop2D: a dark night, a torch that follows your hero, soft shadows under the characters and a day that turns into night by itself. No code.
h1: How to add lights, shadows and a day and night cycle?
carte: Darken the game, light a torch and let the day pass.
etapes: Add the node "Darkness and light mood".
Tick "Shadow under the object" in the Inspector.
Add the node "Day and night cycle".
blocs: With a few nodes, a game goes from flat to atmospheric: a dark night, a lantern that follows your hero, soft shadows and a sun that sets by itself. Nothing to write: you only choose values. The lights are drawn on the screen (they do not go around walls), which keeps the game fast on every phone.
a project open in the editor;
images that look good in the dark (the 3D packs of the library, for example). A pixel art image enlarged a lot looks blurry: turn on **Pixel art** in the game settings.
Choose the **darkness**: 0 is full day, 100 is pitch black. For a night where you still see the scene, try 85.
Choose the **color of the night**: a dark blue looks natural, black makes it scarier.
The darkness and the color change smoothly. Use a length of 30 seconds to turn a day into a night, like a sunset.
Add [[lumiere_source]] and choose the object that carries the light: a torch, a window, a lantern.
Set the **radius** (the distance from the center, in pixels), the **lighting** (100 is normal, up to 300 for a stronger light) and the **colored glow**.
Choose the **flicker**: candle for a soft flame, torch for a strong one, flickers for a failing lamp.
The light follows its object. To make a lantern that follows your hero, put a small invisible object on the hero (a child object) and light that object.
With **Switching on = Only when it is dark**, the light turns on by itself when the night falls and turns off during the day. Use [[lumiere_eteindre]] to turn a light off with a node.
Select a character in the scene and open the **Inspector**, part **Appearance**.
Tick **Shadow under the object**: set its **strength** and its **width**.
The shadow follows the object everywhere. The node [[ombre_objet]] does the same, if you prefer to switch it on during the game.
Add [[lumiere_cycle]] at the start of the game.
Choose the **length of a full day**: 30 to 120 seconds feel alive. Then the **starting moment** (full day, evening, deep night or dawn) and whether it **repeats forever**.
Put your lights on **Only when it is dark**: they turn on at nightfall, all by themselves.

Length 0 stops the cycle where it is. A game on pause freezes the cycle too. To jump to a moment, use [[lumiere_cycle]] again with another starting moment: the example "Day and night village" does it with 5 buttons.
Open the models **Torch and shadows** and **Day and night** (Models tab) to see everything already set up.
Download the example **Day and night village** (Examples tab): a 3D village, windows that light up at night and a knight with a lantern.
Up to 8 lights can shine at the same time, so the game stays fast on every device.
**I do not see any light:** the darkness is probably 0. A light only shows on a darker scene.
**The light does not follow my hero:** attach it to an object placed on the hero (a child object), not to a fixed object.
**The night is not dark enough:** raise the darkness (up to 100) and choose a darker color.
